title: sum_list
summary: Add up every number in a list.
rules: Must be tail recursive.
Don't use any List library functions.
hint: Carry the running total in an extra argument.

practice.starter:
let sum_list (l : int list) : int =
  failwith "sum_list: fill me in"
practice.solution:
let sum_list (l : int list) : int =
  let rec loop (l : int list) (acc : int) : int =
    begin match l with
    | [] -> acc
    | x :: tl -> loop tl (acc + x)
    end
  in
  loop l 0
practice.nonTail:
let rec sum_list (l : int list) : int =
  begin match l with
  | [] -> 0
  | x :: tl -> x + sum_list tl
  end
practice.tests:
;; run_test "empty list sums to 0" (fun () ->
  sum_list [] = 0)
;; run_test "sum_list [1; 2; 3] = 6" (fun () ->
  sum_list [1; 2; 3] = 6)
;; run_test "negative numbers" (fun () ->
  sum_list [5; -2; -3] = 0)
;; run_test "one element" (fun () ->
  sum_list [42] = 42)
;; run_test "tail recursive: a very long list of ones" (fun () ->
  sum_list (tr_init stress_n (fun _ -> 1)) = stress_n)

title: count_if
summary: Count how many elements of a list satisfy a predicate.
rules: Must be tail recursive.
Don't use any List library functions.

practice.starter:
let count_if (p : 'a -> bool) (l : 'a list) : int =
  failwith "count_if: fill me in"
practice.solution:
let count_if (p : 'a -> bool) (l : 'a list) : int =
  let rec loop (l : 'a list) (acc : int) : int =
    begin match l with
    | [] -> acc
    | x :: tl -> loop tl (if p x then acc + 1 else acc)
    end
  in
  loop l 0
practice.nonTail:
let rec count_if (p : 'a -> bool) (l : 'a list) : int =
  begin match l with
  | [] -> 0
  | x :: tl -> (if p x then 1 else 0) + count_if p tl
  end
practice.tests:
;; run_test "empty list counts 0" (fun () ->
  count_if (fun _ -> true) [] = 0)
;; run_test "count_if (fun x -> x > 2) [1; 3; 5] = 2" (fun () ->
  count_if (fun x -> x > 2) [1; 3; 5] = 2)
;; run_test "nothing matches" (fun () ->
  count_if (fun x -> x < 0) [1; 2; 3] = 0)
;; run_test "works on strings" (fun () ->
  count_if (fun s -> s = "a") ["a"; "b"; "a"] = 2)
;; run_test "tail recursive: counts the even numbers in a very long list" (fun () ->
  count_if (fun x -> x mod 2 = 0) (tr_init stress_n (fun i -> i)) = stress_n / 2)

title: max_list
summary: Return the largest number in a list, or None if the list is empty.
signature: val max_list : int list -> int option
rules: Must be tail recursive.
Don't use any List library functions.
hint: Start the accumulator at the first element, not at 0.

practice.starter:
let max_list (l : int list) : int option =
  failwith "max_list: fill me in"
practice.solution:
let max_list (l : int list) : int option =
  let rec loop (l : int list) (best : int) : int =
    begin match l with
    | [] -> best
    | x :: tl -> loop tl (if x > best then x else best)
    end
  in
  begin match l with
  | [] -> None
  | x :: tl -> Some (loop tl x)
  end
practice.nonTail:
let rec max_list (l : int list) : int option =
  begin match l with
  | [] -> None
  | x :: tl ->
    begin match max_list tl with
    | None -> Some x
    | Some m -> Some (if x > m then x else m)
    end
  end
practice.tests:
;; run_test "empty list gives None" (fun () ->
  max_list [] = None)
;; run_test "max_list [3; 9; 2] = Some 9" (fun () ->
  max_list [3; 9; 2] = Some 9)
;; run_test "all negative numbers" (fun () ->
  max_list [-5; -2; -9] = Some (-2))
;; run_test "largest at the end" (fun () ->
  max_list [1; 2; 3; 10] = Some 10)
;; run_test "tail recursive: a very long increasing list" (fun () ->
  max_list (tr_init stress_n (fun i -> i)) = Some (stress_n - 1))

title: reverse
summary: Reverse a list.
rules: Must be tail recursive.
Don't use any List library functions. No @ either.
hint: Moving elements one at a time onto an accumulator reverses them for free.

practice.starter:
let reverse (l : 'a list) : 'a list =
  failwith "reverse: fill me in"
practice.solution:
let reverse (l : 'a list) : 'a list =
  let rec loop (l : 'a list) (acc : 'a list) : 'a list =
    begin match l with
    | [] -> acc
    | x :: tl -> loop tl (x :: acc)
    end
  in
  loop l []
practice.nonTail:
let rec reverse (l : 'a list) : 'a list =
  let rec snoc (l : 'a list) (y : 'a) : 'a list =
    begin match l with [] -> [y] | x :: tl -> x :: snoc tl y end in
  begin match l with
  | [] -> []
  | x :: tl -> snoc (reverse tl) x
  end
practice.tests:
;; run_test "empty list" (fun () ->
  reverse [] = [])
;; run_test "reverse [1; 2; 3] = [3; 2; 1]" (fun () ->
  reverse [1; 2; 3] = [3; 2; 1])
;; run_test "one element" (fun () ->
  reverse ["x"] = ["x"])
;; run_test "reversing twice gives the original" (fun () ->
  reverse (reverse [4; 5; 6; 7]) = [4; 5; 6; 7])
;; run_test "tail recursive: a very long list" (fun () ->
  reverse (tr_init stress_n (fun i -> i)) = List.rev (tr_init stress_n (fun i -> i)))

title: append_tr
summary: Join two lists: every element of l1, in order, followed by every element of l2.
rules: Must be tail recursive.
Don't use @. You may use List.rev, but no other List functions.
hint: Reverse l1 once, then move its elements onto l2 one by one.

practice.starter:
let append_tr (l1 : 'a list) (l2 : 'a list) : 'a list =
  failwith "append_tr: fill me in"
practice.solution:
let append_tr (l1 : 'a list) (l2 : 'a list) : 'a list =
  let rec loop (rev1 : 'a list) (acc : 'a list) : 'a list =
    begin match rev1 with
    | [] -> acc
    | x :: tl -> loop tl (x :: acc)
    end
  in
  loop (List.rev l1) l2
practice.nonTail:
let rec append_tr (l1 : 'a list) (l2 : 'a list) : 'a list =
  begin match l1 with
  | [] -> l2
  | x :: tl -> x :: append_tr tl l2
  end
practice.tests:
;; run_test "both empty" (fun () ->
  append_tr [] [] = [])
;; run_test "append_tr [1; 2] [3; 4] = [1; 2; 3; 4]" (fun () ->
  append_tr [1; 2] [3; 4] = [1; 2; 3; 4])
;; run_test "empty first list" (fun () ->
  append_tr [] [5] = [5])
;; run_test "empty second list keeps the order" (fun () ->
  append_tr [1; 2; 3] [] = [1; 2; 3])
;; run_test "tail recursive: a very long first list" (fun () ->
  List.length (append_tr (tr_init stress_n (fun i -> i)) [0]) = stress_n + 1)

title: map_tr
summary: Apply f to every element of a list and return the results in the same order.
rules: Must be tail recursive.
You may use List.rev, but no other List functions.
hint: The accumulator collects results backwards; reverse it once at the end.

practice.starter:
let map_tr (f : 'a -> 'b) (l : 'a list) : 'b list =
  failwith "map_tr: fill me in"
practice.solution:
let map_tr (f : 'a -> 'b) (l : 'a list) : 'b list =
  let rec loop (l : 'a list) (acc : 'b list) : 'b list =
    begin match l with
    | [] -> List.rev acc
    | x :: tl -> loop tl (f x :: acc)
    end
  in
  loop l []
practice.nonTail:
let rec map_tr (f : 'a -> 'b) (l : 'a list) : 'b list =
  begin match l with
  | [] -> []
  | x :: tl -> let y = f x in y :: map_tr f tl
  end
practice.tests:
;; run_test "empty list" (fun () ->
  map_tr (fun x -> x + 1) [] = [])
;; run_test "keeps the order" (fun () ->
  map_tr (fun x -> x * 10) [1; 2; 3] = [10; 20; 30])
;; run_test "changes the type" (fun () ->
  map_tr string_of_int [7; 8] = ["7"; "8"])
;; run_test "calls f from left to right" (fun () ->
  let seen = ref [] in ignore (map_tr (fun x -> seen := x :: !seen; x) [1; 2; 3]); !seen = [3; 2; 1])
;; run_test "tail recursive: a very long list" (fun () ->
  map_tr (fun x -> x + 1) (tr_init stress_n (fun i -> i)) = tr_init stress_n (fun i -> i + 1))

title: filter_tr
summary: Keep only the elements that satisfy p, in their original order.
rules: Must be tail recursive.
You may use List.rev, but no other List functions.

practice.starter:
let filter_tr (p : 'a -> bool) (l : 'a list) : 'a list =
  failwith "filter_tr: fill me in"
practice.solution:
let filter_tr (p : 'a -> bool) (l : 'a list) : 'a list =
  let rec loop (l : 'a list) (acc : 'a list) : 'a list =
    begin match l with
    | [] -> List.rev acc
    | x :: tl -> loop tl (if p x then x :: acc else acc)
    end
  in
  loop l []
practice.nonTail:
let rec filter_tr (p : 'a -> bool) (l : 'a list) : 'a list =
  begin match l with
  | [] -> []
  | x :: tl -> if p x then x :: filter_tr p tl else filter_tr p tl
  end
practice.tests:
;; run_test "empty list" (fun () ->
  filter_tr (fun _ -> true) [] = [])
;; run_test "keeps the evens in order" (fun () ->
  filter_tr (fun x -> x mod 2 = 0) [1; 2; 3; 4] = [2; 4])
;; run_test "keeps everything" (fun () ->
  filter_tr (fun _ -> true) [3; 1; 2] = [3; 1; 2])
;; run_test "keeps nothing" (fun () ->
  filter_tr (fun _ -> false) [3; 1; 2] = [])
;; run_test "tail recursive: a very long list" (fun () ->
  filter_tr (fun x -> x >= 0) (tr_init stress_n (fun i -> i)) = tr_init stress_n (fun i -> i))

title: range
summary: Build the list of integers from lo up to hi, inclusive. If lo > hi the list is empty.
signature: val range : int -> int -> int list
rules: Must be tail recursive.
Don't use any List library functions. Don't reverse anything at the end.
hint: Count down from hi so each new number goes on the front.

practice.starter:
let range (lo : int) (hi : int) : int list =
  failwith "range: fill me in"
practice.nonTail:
let rec range (lo : int) (hi : int) : int list =
  if lo > hi then [] else lo :: range (lo + 1) hi
practice.tests:
;; run_test "range 2 5 = [2; 3; 4; 5]" (fun () ->
  range 2 5 = [2; 3; 4; 5])
;; run_test "empty when lo > hi" (fun () ->
  range 3 1 = [])
;; run_test "a single number" (fun () ->
  range 7 7 = [7])
;; run_test "negative numbers" (fun () ->
  range (-2) 1 = [-2; -1; 0; 1])
;; run_test "tail recursive: a very long range" (fun () ->
  range 0 (stress_n - 1) = tr_init stress_n (fun i -> i))

title: zip
summary: Pair up the elements of two lists position by position. Stop when the shorter list runs out.
rules: Must be tail recursive.
You may use List.rev, but no other List functions.

practice.starter:
let zip (l1 : 'a list) (l2 : 'b list) : ('a * 'b) list =
  failwith "zip: fill me in"
practice.solution:
let zip (l1 : 'a list) (l2 : 'b list) : ('a * 'b) list =
  let rec loop (l1 : 'a list) (l2 : 'b list) (acc : ('a * 'b) list) : ('a * 'b) list =
    begin match l1, l2 with
    | x :: t1, y :: t2 -> loop t1 t2 ((x, y) :: acc)
    | _ -> List.rev acc
    end
  in
  loop l1 l2 []
practice.nonTail:
let rec zip (l1 : 'a list) (l2 : 'b list) : ('a * 'b) list =
  begin match l1, l2 with
  | x :: t1, y :: t2 -> (x, y) :: zip t1 t2
  | _ -> []
  end
practice.tests:
;; run_test "both empty" (fun () ->
  zip [] [] = ([] : (int * int) list))
;; run_test "same length keeps the order" (fun () ->
  zip [1; 2; 3] ["a"; "b"; "c"] = [(1, "a"); (2, "b"); (3, "c")])
;; run_test "stops at the shorter second list" (fun () ->
  zip [1; 2; 3] ["a"; "b"] = [(1, "a"); (2, "b")])
;; run_test "stops at the shorter first list" (fun () ->
  zip [1] [true; false] = [(1, true)])
;; run_test "tail recursive: two very long lists" (fun () ->
  List.length (zip (tr_init stress_n (fun i -> i)) (tr_init stress_n (fun i -> i))) = stress_n)

title: split_parity
summary: Split a list into its even numbers and its odd numbers, keeping each group in its original order.
signature: val split_parity : int list -> int list * int list
rules: Must be tail recursive.
You may use List.rev, but no other List functions.
hint: Use two accumulators, one per group.

practice.starter:
let split_parity (l : int list) : int list * int list =
  failwith "split_parity: fill me in"
practice.solution:
let split_parity (l : int list) : int list * int list =
  let rec loop (l : int list) (evens : int list) (odds : int list) : int list * int list =
    begin match l with
    | [] -> (List.rev evens, List.rev odds)
    | x :: tl -> if x mod 2 = 0 then loop tl (x :: evens) odds else loop tl evens (x :: odds)
    end
  in
  loop l [] []
practice.nonTail:
let rec split_parity (l : int list) : int list * int list =
  begin match l with
  | [] -> ([], [])
  | x :: tl ->
    let (evens, odds) = split_parity tl in
    if x mod 2 = 0 then (x :: evens, odds) else (evens, x :: odds)
  end
practice.tests:
;; run_test "empty list" (fun () ->
  split_parity [] = ([], []))
;; run_test "split_parity [1; 2; 3; 4; 5] = ([2; 4], [1; 3; 5])" (fun () ->
  split_parity [1; 2; 3; 4; 5] = ([2; 4], [1; 3; 5]))
;; run_test "all even" (fun () ->
  split_parity [8; 6; 4] = ([8; 6; 4], []))
;; run_test "negative odd numbers" (fun () ->
  split_parity [-3; 0] = ([0], [-3]))
;; run_test "tail recursive: a very long list" (fun () ->
  let (e, o) = split_parity (tr_init stress_n (fun i -> i)) in List.length e = stress_n / 2 && List.length o = stress_n / 2)

title: flatten
summary: Join a list of lists into one list, keeping every element in order.
rules: Must be tail recursive.
You may use List.rev, but no other List functions.
hint: Walk the current inner list and the outer list with the same loop.

practice.starter:
let flatten (ls : 'a list list) : 'a list =
  failwith "flatten: fill me in"
practice.solution:
let flatten (ls : 'a list list) : 'a list =
  let rec loop (ls : 'a list list) (cur : 'a list) (acc : 'a list) : 'a list =
    begin match cur with
    | x :: tl -> loop ls tl (x :: acc)
    | [] ->
      begin match ls with
      | [] -> List.rev acc
      | l :: rest -> loop rest l acc
      end
    end
  in
  loop ls [] []
practice.nonTail:
let rec flatten (ls : 'a list list) : 'a list =
  let rec app (l : 'a list) (rest : 'a list) : 'a list =
    begin match l with [] -> rest | x :: tl -> x :: app tl rest end in
  begin match ls with
  | [] -> []
  | l :: rest -> app l (flatten rest)
  end
practice.tests:
;; run_test "no lists" (fun () ->
  flatten ([] : int list list) = [])
;; run_test "flatten [[1; 2]; []; [3]] = [1; 2; 3]" (fun () ->
  flatten [[1; 2]; []; [3]] = [1; 2; 3])
;; run_test "only empty lists" (fun () ->
  flatten [[]; []] = ([] : int list))
;; run_test "keeps the order inside and across lists" (fun () ->
  flatten [["a"]; ["b"; "c"]; ["d"]] = ["a"; "b"; "c"; "d"])
;; run_test "tail recursive: very many short lists" (fun () ->
  flatten (tr_init stress_n (fun i -> [i])) = tr_init stress_n (fun i -> i))
;; run_test "tail recursive: one very long inner list" (fun () ->
  flatten [[]; tr_init stress_n (fun i -> i)] = tr_init stress_n (fun i -> i))

title: merge
summary: Merge two lists that are each sorted in increasing order into one sorted list.
signature: val merge : int list -> int list -> int list
rules: Must be tail recursive.
You may use List.rev, but no other List functions.
hint: When one list runs out, the rest of the other still has to go onto the accumulator.

practice.starter:
let merge (l1 : int list) (l2 : int list) : int list =
  failwith "merge: fill me in"
practice.nonTail:
let rec merge (l1 : int list) (l2 : int list) : int list =
  begin match l1, l2 with
  | [], rest | rest, [] -> rest
  | x :: t1, y :: t2 -> if x <= y then x :: merge t1 l2 else y :: merge l1 t2
  end
practice.tests:
;; run_test "both empty" (fun () ->
  merge [] [] = [])
;; run_test "merge [1; 4; 6] [2; 3; 7] = [1; 2; 3; 4; 6; 7]" (fun () ->
  merge [1; 4; 6] [2; 3; 7] = [1; 2; 3; 4; 6; 7])
;; run_test "one side empty" (fun () ->
  merge [] [2; 5] = [2; 5] && merge [2; 5] [] = [2; 5])
;; run_test "keeps duplicates" (fun () ->
  merge [1; 2; 2] [2; 3] = [1; 2; 2; 2; 3])
;; run_test "everything in one list comes first" (fun () ->
  merge [1; 2] [8; 9] = [1; 2; 8; 9])
;; run_test "tail recursive: two very long interleaved lists" (fun () ->
  merge (tr_init (stress_n / 2) (fun i -> 2 * i)) (tr_init (stress_n / 2) (fun i -> 2 * i + 1)) = tr_init stress_n (fun i -> i))

title: fold_right_tr
summary: Write fold_right without growing the stack: fold_right_tr f l base = f x1 (f x2 (... (f xn base))).
rules: Must be tail recursive.
You may use List.rev, but no other List functions.
hint: Reversing the list first lets you apply f in the right order with an accumulator.

practice.starter:
let fold_right_tr (f : 'a -> 'b -> 'b) (l : 'a list) (base : 'b) : 'b =
  failwith "fold_right_tr: fill me in"
practice.solution:
let fold_right_tr (f : 'a -> 'b -> 'b) (l : 'a list) (base : 'b) : 'b =
  let rec loop (rev : 'a list) (acc : 'b) : 'b =
    begin match rev with
    | [] -> acc
    | x :: tl -> loop tl (f x acc)
    end
  in
  loop (List.rev l) base
practice.nonTail:
let rec fold_right_tr (f : 'a -> 'b -> 'b) (l : 'a list) (base : 'b) : 'b =
  begin match l with
  | [] -> base
  | x :: tl -> f x (fold_right_tr f tl base)
  end
practice.tests:
;; run_test "empty list returns base" (fun () ->
  fold_right_tr (fun x acc -> x + acc) [] 5 = 5)
;; run_test "rebuilds the list in order" (fun () ->
  fold_right_tr (fun x acc -> x :: acc) [1; 2; 3] [] = [1; 2; 3])
;; run_test "applies f to the last element first" (fun () ->
  fold_right_tr (fun x acc -> acc ^ x) ["a"; "b"; "c"] "" = "cba")
;; run_test "non-commutative f" (fun () ->
  fold_right_tr (fun x acc -> acc - x) [1; 2] 10 = 7)
;; run_test "tail recursive: a very long list" (fun () ->
  fold_right_tr (fun x acc -> x :: acc) (tr_init stress_n (fun i -> i)) [] = tr_init stress_n (fun i -> i))

title: encode
summary: Run-length encode a list: replace each run of equal neighbours with (value, how many times it repeats).
rules: Must be tail recursive.
You may use List.rev, but no other List functions.
hint: Keep the current value and its count in the accumulator alongside the finished runs.

practice.starter:
let encode (l : 'a list) : ('a * int) list =
  failwith "encode: fill me in"
practice.solution:
let encode (l : 'a list) : ('a * int) list =
  let rec loop (l : 'a list) (cur : 'a) (n : int) (acc : ('a * int) list) : ('a * int) list =
    begin match l with
    | [] -> List.rev ((cur, n) :: acc)
    | x :: tl -> if x = cur then loop tl cur (n + 1) acc else loop tl x 1 ((cur, n) :: acc)
    end
  in
  begin match l with
  | [] -> []
  | x :: tl -> loop tl x 1 []
  end
practice.nonTail:
let rec encode (l : 'a list) : ('a * int) list =
  begin match l with
  | [] -> []
  | x :: tl ->
    begin match encode tl with
    | (y, n) :: rest when y = x -> (x, n + 1) :: rest
    | rest -> (x, 1) :: rest
    end
  end
practice.tests:
;; run_test "empty list" (fun () ->
  encode ([] : int list) = [])
;; run_test "runs of letters" (fun () ->
  encode ["a"; "a"; "b"; "a"] = [("a", 2); ("b", 1); ("a", 1)])
;; run_test "one long run" (fun () ->
  encode [7; 7; 7] = [(7, 3)])
;; run_test "no repeats" (fun () ->
  encode [1; 2; 3] = [(1, 1); (2, 1); (3, 1)])
;; run_test "tail recursive: a very long list of pairs" (fun () ->
  encode (tr_init stress_n (fun i -> i / 2)) = tr_init (stress_n / 2) (fun i -> (i, 2)))

title: fib
summary: Compute the nth Fibonacci number (fib 0 = 0, fib 1 = 1) in linear time.
rules: Must be tail recursive.
Must take linear time: no double recursion.
hint: Carry two consecutive Fibonacci numbers in the accumulators.

practice.starter:
let fib (n : int) : int =
  failwith "fib: fill me in"
practice.tests:
;; run_test "fib 0 = 0" (fun () ->
  fib 0 = 0)
;; run_test "fib 1 = 1" (fun () ->
  fib 1 = 1)
;; run_test "fib 10 = 55" (fun () ->
  fib 10 = 55)
;; run_test "fib 30 = 832040" (fun () ->
  fib 30 = 832040)

  let a = ref 0 and b = ref 1 in for _ = 1 to stress_n do let c = !a + !b in a := !b; b := c done; fib stress_n = !a)

title: apply_n
summary: Apply f to x, n times in a row. apply_n f 0 x = x.
rules: Must be tail recursive.
hint: f x can be computed before the recursive call instead of after.

practice.starter:
let apply_n (f : 'a -> 'a) (n : int) (x : 'a) : 'a =
  failwith "apply_n: fill me in"
practice.solution:
let rec apply_n (f : 'a -> 'a) (n : int) (x : 'a) : 'a =
  if n <= 0 then x else apply_n f (n - 1) (f x)
practice.nonTail:
let rec apply_n (f : 'a -> 'a) (n : int) (x : 'a) : 'a =
  if n <= 0 then x else f (apply_n f (n - 1) x)
practice.tests:
;; run_test "zero times returns x" (fun () ->
  apply_n (fun x -> x + 1) 0 5 = 5)
;; run_test "apply_n (fun x -> x * 2) 3 1 = 8" (fun () ->
  apply_n (fun x -> x * 2) 3 1 = 8)
;; run_test "works on strings" (fun () ->
  apply_n (fun s -> s ^ "!") 2 "hi" = "hi!!")
;; run_test "order matters for lists" (fun () ->
  apply_n (fun l -> List.length l :: l) 3 [] = [2; 1; 0])
;; run_test "tail recursive: a very large n" (fun () ->
  apply_n (fun x -> x + 1) stress_n 0 = stress_n)

title: size
summary: Count the nodes of a binary tree without growing the stack, using a list of trees still to visit (a worklist).
signature:
type 'a tree = Empty | Node of 'a tree * 'a * 'a tree
val size : 'a tree -> int
rules: Must be tail recursive.
Very deep, one-sided trees must work too.
hint: A tree list replaces the call stack: pop one, push its children.

practice.starter:
let size (t : 'a tree) : int =
  failwith "size: fill me in"
practice.solution:
let size (t : 'a tree) : int =
  let rec loop (todo : 'a tree list) (acc : int) : int =
    begin match todo with
    | [] -> acc
    | Empty :: rest -> loop rest acc
    | Node (l, _, r) :: rest -> loop (l :: r :: rest) (acc + 1)
    end
  in
  loop [t] 0
practice.nonTail:
let rec size (t : 'a tree) : int =
  begin match t with
  | Empty -> 0
  | Node (l, _, r) -> size l + 1 + size r
  end
practice.tests:
;; run_test "empty tree" (fun () ->
  size Empty = 0)
;; run_test "one node" (fun () ->
  size (Node (Empty, "x", Empty)) = 1)
;; run_test "the sample tree has 6 nodes" (fun () ->
  size sample = 6)
;; run_test "tail recursive: a very deep tree leaning left" (fun () ->
  size (left_chain stress_n) = stress_n)
;; run_test "tail recursive: a very deep tree leaning right" (fun () ->
  size (right_chain stress_n) = stress_n)

title: inorder
summary: List the values of a binary tree in order (left subtree, then the node, then the right subtree), using an explicit stack instead of recursion on both children.
signature:
type 'a tree = Empty | Node of 'a tree * 'a * 'a tree
val inorder : 'a tree -> 'a list
rules: Must be tail recursive.
You may use List.rev, but no other List functions.
Very deep, one-sided trees must work too.
hint: Walk left as far as you can, remembering each node you pass on a stack.

practice.starter:
let inorder (t : 'a tree) : 'a list =
  failwith "inorder: fill me in"
practice.solution:
let inorder (t : 'a tree) : 'a list =
  (* stack holds nodes whose left side is done but whose value isn't listed yet *)
  let rec loop (cur : 'a tree) (stack : ('a * 'a tree) list) (acc : 'a list) : 'a list =
    begin match cur with
    | Node (l, v, r) -> loop l ((v, r) :: stack) acc
    | Empty ->
      begin match stack with
      | [] -> List.rev acc
      | (v, r) :: rest -> loop r rest (v :: acc)
      end
    end
  in
  loop t [] []
practice.nonTail:
let rec inorder (t : 'a tree) : 'a list =
  let rec app (l : 'a list) (rest : 'a list) : 'a list =
    begin match l with [] -> rest | x :: tl -> x :: app tl rest end in
  begin match t with
  | Empty -> []
  | Node (l, v, r) -> app (inorder l) (v :: inorder r)
  end
practice.tests:
;; run_test "empty tree" (fun () ->
  inorder Empty = ([] : int list))
;; run_test "one node" (fun () ->
  inorder (Node (Empty, 5, Empty)) = [5])
;; run_test "the sample tree lists 1 to 6" (fun () ->
  inorder sample = [1; 2; 3; 4; 5; 6])
;; run_test "a left-leaning tree" (fun () ->
  inorder (left_chain 4) = [1; 2; 3; 4])
;; run_test "tail recursive: a very deep tree leaning left" (fun () ->
  inorder (left_chain stress_n) = tr_init stress_n (fun i -> i + 1))
;; run_test "tail recursive: a very deep tree leaning right" (fun () ->
  inorder (right_chain stress_n) = tr_init stress_n (fun i -> i + 1))

title: contains
summary: Return true if some element of the queue equals x. Stop as soon as you find it.
rules: Must be tail recursive.
The queue types are the ones from Homework 4. Use only create and enq, plus your own helpers.
Exit early: return as soon as you find x.
hint: In b1 || b2, only b2 is in tail position. Which side should the recursive call go on?

practice.starter:
let contains (x : 'a) (q : 'a queue) : bool =
  failwith "contains: fill me in"
practice.solution:
let contains (x : 'a) (q : 'a queue) : bool =
  let rec loop (no : 'a qnode option) : bool =
    begin match no with
    | None -> false
    | Some n -> n.v = x || loop n.next
    end
  in
  loop q.head
practice.nonTail:
let contains (x : 'a) (q : 'a queue) : bool =
  let rec loop (no : 'a qnode option) : bool =
    begin match no with
    | None -> false
    | Some n -> loop n.next || n.v = x
    end
  in
  loop q.head

title: index_of
summary: Return Some i where i is the position (counting from 0 at the head) of the first element equal to x, or None if x is not in the queue.
rules: Must be tail recursive.
The queue types are the ones from Homework 4. Use only create and enq, plus your own helpers.
Exit early: stop at the first match.
hint: Count positions on the way down instead of adding 1 on the way back up.

practice.starter:
let index_of (x : 'a) (q : 'a queue) : int option =
  failwith "index_of: fill me in"
practice.solution:
let index_of (x : 'a) (q : 'a queue) : int option =
  let rec loop (no : 'a qnode option) (i : int) : int option =
    begin match no with
    | None -> None
    | Some n -> if n.v = x then Some i else loop n.next (i + 1)
    end
  in
  loop q.head 0
practice.nonTail:
let index_of (x : 'a) (q : 'a queue) : int option =
  let rec loop (no : 'a qnode option) : int option =
    begin match no with
    | None -> None
    | Some n ->
      if n.v = x then Some 0
      else begin match loop n.next with
        | None -> None
        | Some i -> Some (i + 1)
      end
    end
  in
  loop q.head
practice.tests:
;; run_test "empty queue" (fun () ->
  index_of 1 (create ()) = None)
;; run_test "the head is at 0" (fun () ->
  index_of "a" (q_of_list ["a"; "b"; "c"]) = Some 0)
;; run_test "the last element" (fun () ->
  index_of "c" (q_of_list ["a"; "b"; "c"]) = Some 2)
;; run_test "the first of several matches" (fun () ->
  index_of 7 (q_of_list [1; 7; 2; 7]) = Some 1)
;; run_test "missing element" (fun () ->
  index_of "z" (q_of_list ["a"; "b"]) = None)
;; run_test "tail recursive: the last element of a very long queue" (fun () ->
  index_of (stress_n - 1) (q_of_list (tr_init stress_n (fun i -> i))) = Some (stress_n - 1))

title: remove_all
summary: Remove every node whose value equals x from the queue, in place. The remaining nodes must be the same nodes as before, still in order, and the queue must stay valid.
examples: after remove_all 1 on 1, 2, 1, 3 the queue is 2, 3
rules: Must be tail recursive.
The queue types are the ones from Homework 4. Use only create and enq, plus your own helpers.
Don't allocate new nodes: relink the existing ones.
Remember to fix head and tail.
hint: Carry the last node you kept so you can link around the removed ones.

practice.starter:
let remove_all (x : 'a) (q : 'a queue) : unit =
  failwith "remove_all: fill me in"
practice.solution:
let remove_all (x : 'a) (q : 'a queue) : unit =
  (* prev is the last node kept so far *)
  let rec loop (prev : 'a qnode option) (cur : 'a qnode option) : unit =
    begin match cur with
    | None -> q.tail <- prev
    | Some n ->
      if n.v = x then begin
        (match prev with None -> q.head <- n.next | Some p -> p.next <- n.next);
        loop prev n.next
      end
      else loop cur n.next
    end
  in
  loop None q.head

title: count
summary: Count how many elements of a deque satisfy p.
rules: Must be tail recursive.
The deque types are the ones from Homework 4.

practice.starter:
let count (p : 'a -> bool) (d : 'a deque) : int =
  failwith "count: fill me in"
practice.solution:
let count (p : 'a -> bool) (d : 'a deque) : int =
  let rec loop (no : 'a dqnode option) (acc : int) : int =
    begin match no with
    | None -> acc
    | Some n -> loop n.next (if p n.v then acc + 1 else acc)
    end
  in
  loop d.head 0
practice.nonTail:
let count (p : 'a -> bool) (d : 'a deque) : int =
  let rec loop (no : 'a dqnode option) : int =
    begin match no with
    | None -> 0
    | Some n -> (if p n.v then 1 else 0) + loop n.next
    end
  in
  loop d.head

  count (fun _ -> true) (create ()) = 0)
